briefs.caption:
Playoff chaos in Florida. ⚽😱

#8 seed Miami FC knocked out the #1 seed and Players’ Shield winners, the Tampa Bay Rowdies, in the USL Championship Eastern Conference Quarterfinal at Al Lang Stadium.

1-1 after extra time: Matias Romero scored for Miami in the 34th minute, MD Myers answered for Tampa Bay in the 44th, and Myers had a penalty saved late in extra time. Miami won the shootout 5-4.

“That’s playoff football for you.” — Rowdies head coach Dominic Casciato

Our take: this is why you watch live. Follow Cancha for Miami FC’s next round.

briefs.caption:
A pro club wants to put $350K into college fields ⚽🏟️

Fort Lauderdale United FC and Broward College announced a proposal for an estimated $350,000 in upgrades at Broward College's Central Campus: baseball fields converted into multipurpose soccer fields, new grass, upgraded irrigation and restored field lighting.

Broward College students and intramurals get first priority. FTL UTD would get space for youth development, clinics, training and community events.

Our take: more lit, soccer-ready fields means more room for youth programs and pickup in Broward. It's still a proposal, so we'll be watching for construction dates.

Source: Fort Lauderdale United FC, Oct 29, 2026 (ftlutd.com).

briefs.caption:
Your kid's age group changed this season. Here's why. 👇

For 2026-27, US Youth Soccer, US Club Soccer and AYSO moved youth soccer from birth-year to school-year age groups: August 1 to July 31 instead of January to December.

Example: U-12 is now born Aug 1, 2014 to Jul 31, 2015. Born August to December? Your player likely moves to a younger age group than under the old rule. Born January to July? Same group as before.

Leagues could choose their system, so confirm your league's chart and ask clubs which age group your player tries out for.

🧮 Find your player's 2026-27 age group, ODP range and college contact date in seconds: link in bio → Pathway → Your soccer timeline.

18 Florida entries are on Chobani's Feed the Dream winners list 💰⚽

Chobani's Feed the Dream program is giving $10,000 grants to youth soccer clubs. Its winners list so far includes:

South Florida: Albion SC Miami, Fort Lauderdale Rush FC, GOT FC, Miami SCORES, Parkland Travel Soccer Club, WASA SC
Central Florida: BlackLions SC, Florida Kraze Krush, Orlando Soccer School Lake Nona, PSG Academy Orlando
Tampa Bay, Southwest & Panhandle: Tampa Dynamo FC, Warriors Soccer Academy, Mutiny SC, Lakewood Ranch FC, North Port Youth Soccer, Cape Coral Soccer Association (two programs), Gulfsouth Soccer Club

Chobani notes that winners are still being verified, so the final list may change.

Our take: money for local clubs is real, and it goes to clubs that apply. Club leaders, follow Cancha for the next grant alert. Congrats to every Florida club on the list 👏
